dasProblem.title: As long as F&B depends on one person, it's your biggest risk.

F&B determines the profitability of your property while remaining its most unreliable component.

modal.headline: Robotic Gastronomy – a new operating system for gastronomy.
modal.intro1: Gastronomy is facing a structural transformation. Over 60,000 open positions, rising labor costs, and growing margin pressure make it clear: the existing operating model is reaching its limits.
modal.intro2: Robotic Gastronomy is the answer. Not as a single technology, but as an integrated operating system built on four pillars:

pillars.title: Automation
pillars.text: Robotics takes over recurring processes in the kitchen, logistics, and service. The result: consistent quality, less dependency on staff, predictable workflows.

pillars.title: Digitalization
pillars.text: Fully networked systems connect ordering, production, and guest retention. Every process becomes measurable and controllable.

pillars.title: AI Integration
pillars.text: Artificial intelligence enables forecasts for revenue, cost of goods, and expenses. Planning replaces gut feeling.

pillars.title: Scalability
pillars.text: Together, these disciplines make gastronomy reproducible – across locations, without complexity and costs growing proportionally.

modal.outro1: Cooking robotics is already being used today by companies such as REWE, Mercedes-Benz, and the German armed forces. The market is growing at around 20% annually. The technology is available – what has been missing so far are business models that integrate it economically.
modal.outro2: This is exactly where Robotic Gastronomy comes in: technology not as an end in itself, but as the foundation for gastronomy that works economically – for operators, investors, and guests.

ways.title: Way 1: System Kitchen
ways.description: A system kitchen is a fully standardised kitchen in which workflows, recipes and processes are defined in clear standards (SOPs). The result is consistent quality, predictable costs and low dependency on individuals, because knowledge lives in the system and not just in individual heads.

whenUseful.label: When it makes sense
whenUseful.text: For properties with volatile business that want to standardise quality and profitability.

whenNot.label: When it does not
whenNot.text: When structural and process changes are not desired.

ways.title: Way 2: Hybrid Kitchen
ways.description: A hybrid kitchen combines the standardised processes of a system kitchen with targeted à-la-carte elements. Individual, recurring production processes are systematised through technology and standards, while the team focuses on individual components, quality and the guest experience. It is the bridge between classic à-la-carte and system kitchen.

whenUseful.label: When it makes sense
whenUseful.text: When staff is scarce but a full system kitchen is not yet economically or conceptually feasible.

whenNot.label: When it does not
whenNot.text: When the infrastructure does not allow for adaptation.

ways.title: Way 3: Robotic
ways.description: Robotic means the consistent implementation of automation for 24/7 requirements. Robots handle food preparation fully automatically, embedded in a well-thought-out business model with integrated processes. Important: robotics is not an end in itself or a gimmick, but a lever for productivity and scalability.

whenUseful.label: When it makes sense
whenUseful.text: For locations with constant volume and 24/7 demand for supplying employees and guests.
